concerns.text: Acceptance requires mIoU 'numerically lower than the global-attention baseline' — this presupposes the empirical finding. A sound design must accept a valid measurement either way; if local attention does not degrade mIoU, that IS the result. Same defect in US-2 Scenario 2 ('statistically significant difference... p < 0.05') — significance cannot be an acceptance criterion, only a reported outcome.

Repeated-measures ANOVA is mis-specified for the stated comparison. Sparsity level is within-image (repeated), but dense vs. non-dense scene is a between-image factor — the design requires a two-way mixed (split-plot) ANOVA with an interaction term, not a one-way repeated-measures ANOVA. Also, per-image mIoU is bounded in [0,1] and likely non-normal; the spec should name the assumption check or a non-parametric alternative (e.g., Friedman + aligned-rank test).

'Tipping point' / knee identification is not operationalized. A 4-point grid (Global, 64, 32, 16) cannot localize a knee; no knee-detection method (e.g., max-curvature, piecewise regression) is named, and the ±8-patch sensitivity sweep in Assumptions is mentioned but not required by any FR/SC. As written, 'reveals a non-linear degradation pattern' is unfalsifiable at 4 points.

Attribution comparison is confounded: SC-004 compares heatmaps between successful global-attention runs and failed local-attention runs, so any heatmap difference may reflect prediction correctness rather than reliance on global context. The comparison should hold outcome or condition fixed (e.g., correct predictions under both conditions, or failures under both). Also no quantitative metric for 'spatial distribution of activation' is defined — 'significant activation on global context tokens' is not measurable as stated.

'Ground-truth bounding boxes are themselves ambiguous or poorly annotated' — no criterion is given for how ambiguity of ground truth is detected (vs. the IoU>0.10 rule used for scene density). Flagging rule must be defined or the exclusion is arbitrary.
